recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants a replacement way to declare unknown-extension handling, it should be handled as a new decision rather than as FHIR-7450 follow-up.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 FHIR-I issue asking how systems that do not accept unknown extensions declare that fact; the resolution was merged into Conformance.acceptUnknown rather than a new rejectUnknown element.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn revision 6101. Git commit 578f4a5f5c145453fc3cb71847eb44b247d6d96a maps to build@6101 and changed Conformance.acceptUnknown from boolean to a code bound to UnknownContentCode with values covering unknown elements and extensions.
additional_context: FHIR-8170 was closed as the same concern/duplicate. Later FHIR-14647 removed CapabilityStatement.acceptUnknown because it was awkward and unused, and FHIR-18363 removed the extensibility-page SHALL to declare non-acceptance in CapabilityStatement because the declaration mechanism no longer existed. Current build-scope source reflects those later decisions; combined already contains separate audit commits for FHIR-14647 and FHIR-18363.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because resurrecting rejectUnknown or acceptUnknown would contradict later final FHIR-I decisions, and the active extensibility guidance no longer contains the old declaration requirement.
